attrs.label: Public URL
attrs.description:
The address users open openGym at, without a path or trailing slash.</br>
Passkeys are bound to this hostname and only work over HTTPS,</br>
so behind a reverse proxy use its HTTPS address (for example https://gym.example.com).</br>
For a LAN-only test, the NAS address (for example http://192.168.1.10:30552) works with guest mode or password sign-in.

attrs.label: Passkey Display Name
attrs.description: The name shown in the browser's passkey prompt.

attrs.label: First Profile Becomes Admin
attrs.description: The first profile created on an empty instance gets the admin dashboard.

attrs.label: Invite Only
attrs.description: Require an invite code to create a profile.

attrs.label: Allow Guest Mode
attrs.description: Offer "Continue without account". Disable to require a profile.

attrs.label: Password Sign-in
attrs.description: Offer name-and-password sign-in next to passkeys. Useful when openGym is not served over HTTPS.

attrs.label: Additional Environment Variables
attrs.description:
Additional environment variables for the openGym API</br>
(for example ADMIN_UIDS, SESSION_DAYS, AUDIT_DAYS, DEFAULT_LANG).

attrs.label: User ID

attrs.description: The group id that openGym files will be owned by.

attrs.label: Port Bind Mode
attrs.description:
The port bind mode.</br>
- Publish: The port will be published on the host for external access.</br>
- Expose: The port will be exposed for inter-container communication.</br>
- None: The port will not be exposed or published.</br>
Note: If the Dockerfile defines an EXPOSE directive,
the port will still be exposed for inter-container communication regardless of this setting.

enum.description: Publish port on the host for external access

openGym is a self-hosted gym and body-weight tracker. Plan routines, log workouts, track your weight and progress, and sign in with passkeys.
